get.description: Lists the acting tenant's live communication sessions. Tenant-scoped by specification, shaped at the database by a projection, and OData-shaped through the $-prefixed query string. Gated on communication_sessions_read inside the use case.

post.description: Opens a live session immediately, or schedules one when ScheduledStartUtc is supplied. The frozen lifecycle is Scheduled -> Open -> Ended and Scheduled -> Cancelled; an immediate session is created directly as Open, and state is never derived from a combination of nullable timestamps. Ownership comes from the authenticated caller, never from the payload. Gated on communication_sessions_create. RETURNS THE SESSION IT CREATED: the id read back off the persisted aggregate, the lifecycle state the server chose, and the creation instant. It answers 200 inside the platform envelope rather than 201 with a Location header, because every ABS surface answers in that envelope and every ServiceClient unwraps it; a lone endpoint changing conventions would buy REST purity at the cost of the one convention all of its callers already implement. NO TRUSTED ORIGIN IS ACCEPTED HERE, AND THERE IS NO FIELD FOR ONE. The opaque trusted host-resource label is the authority coordinate an admission decision is composed against and stamped into every evidence row, so ADR-0067 frozen rule 6a requires it to be resolved on the server: a browser saying 'I am admitted to zone X' is never an input. It is a parameter of the in-process command, supplied by a server-side caller that already resolved a host resource, and this endpoint supplies none.

get.description: Counts the acting tenant's live communication sessions over the SAME specification the list uses, so a badge count can never drift from the list it counts. Honours $filter and $search only — paging must never alter a total.
Reads one session by id. The tenant rides IN the lookup rather than being checked afterwards, so a foreign-tenant id is not merely refused — it is not addressable, and the answer is 404.

post.description: Ends an open session for EVERY participant. Ended is terminal — Ended -> Open is refused — so this is not reversible and a new session is the only way back. Gated on communication_sessions_manage rather than _update, because ending affects everybody rather than only the caller.

Cancels a session that has not opened. Cancelling an already-open session is refused by the aggregate with a 409: an open session is ENDED, not cancelled. Gated on communication_sessions_delete — a session row is never deleted, and withdrawing a planned occasion is the closest this aggregate comes to it.

get.description: Lists the session's durable roster. Roster membership is not admission and not presence: it means a principal MAY be evaluated for admission, not that any authority has said yes, and it says nothing about whether they are connected right now. Reached through a parent-bound specification carrying both the session and the tenant, so a participant of another session is not addressable through this one.

post.summary: Add a principal to a session's roster
post.description: Adds a principal to the session's roster in the Invited state. The session id is taken from the loaded parent rather than from the payload, so a body naming a different session cannot smuggle a roster row onto it. Gated on communication_sessions_update. RETURNS THE ROSTER ROW IT CREATED: its id — which is the route segment every later Admit, Deny, Update and Remove call needs — the session it was actually attached to, and the Invited state it was created in. Being on the roster is still not an admission.

get.description: Counts the session's roster over the same parent-bound specification the list uses.

put.description: Changes what a principal on the roster is present to DO. One editable field, and the payload's silences are the design: membership STATE is absent because it moves through guarded roster verbs, each of which refuses an undeclared move — a settable state would let a caller write 'joined' without anybody having joined. The PRINCIPAL is absent because who a roster row is about is its identity; a different principal is a different row. The change is refused with a 409 once the membership is terminal, by the aggregate itself: a left or removed member's role is a historical fact. Gated on communication_sessions_update, matching the invite it edits.

post.summary: Remove a principal from a session's roster
post.description: Moves one membership to the terminal Removed state and records the operator's decision as immutable admission evidence, in ONE commit — so there is never a removed member with no record of who removed them, and never a record of a removal that did not happen. IT IS NOT A DELETE, and it is deliberately not spelled DELETE. Every admission decision carries a required foreign key to the roster row it was taken against, so deleting the row would take the 'why could I not join' trail with it: participation is an auditable record. Terminal means terminal — a returning principal is invited as a NEW row rather than restored into this one, and the aggregate refuses an undeclared move with a 409. Gated on communication_sessions_manage rather than _update, on the same reasoning that gates End: ejecting somebody is administration of the occasion exercised over another person, and a role granted read+update should no more be able to eject a host than to hang up on the room. Returns the admission-evidence row it appended.

THE SELF-LEAVE VERB, and the mirror of Join. The acting principal ends their OWN presence: the roster membership moves to the Left state and one participation fact records the departure, both in ONE commit. IT IS NOT Remove, and the difference is not cosmetic. Remove is EJECTION, gated on communication_sessions_manage, and it writes abs.communications.admission.operator.removed into the admission trail. Borrowing it to hang up gave an ordinary attendee a 403, and had it succeeded it would have recorded a voluntary departure as an ejection by an operator who never acted. LEAVING IS SELF-SCOPED: the executor and the subject are the same principal. The server resolves the acting principal from the caller's own governed identity — never from this route — and refuses a roster row naming anybody else with 403 abs.communications.admission.principal_mismatch, the same frozen token the admission checkpoints raise. The participantId is an ADDRESS, not a claim: naming somebody else's row does not make it leavable, so this endpoint can never become ejection under a friendlier name. Gated on communication_sessions_update — the same coarse gate Admit and Join use, because a room a principal can enter with _update must be a room they can leave with _update. The permission is not the authority; the identity match is, and no grant widens it. NO ADMISSION ROW IS WRITTEN. A departure is not a verdict — nothing was consulted and nobody was refused — so the evidence is a PARTICIPATION fact carrying abs.communications.evidence.participation.self_left. Read it back through /Participation, not through /Admissions. Terminal both ways: leaving an Ended or Cancelled session is a 409, and so is a second departure or a departure from a membership an operator already ended, refused by the aggregate that owns the rule. Returns the membership that is now over and the participation fact that says so.

post.summary: Issue a participant an ephemeral media credential
post.description: THE MEDIA GRANT CHECKPOINT, and it is a SEPARATE call from Join on purpose. Join answers 'is this principal admitted, right now, on current authority'. This answers 'what may they carry, on which vendor resource, under what credential'. A session with no bound provider resource still admits people perfectly well, and a bound resource still refuses a grant to a principal whose membership has ended, so one verb that did both would hide which half failed. THE RESPONSE CARRIES A VENDOR CREDENTIAL. It is minted for this caller, is persisted nowhere in this platform, and is dropped as soon as this response is written. Store it nowhere and log it nowhere. STATUS IS ALWAYS 'media authorized' AND NEVER 'media connected'. Holding this proves the bearer was AUTHORIZED to exchange media; it proves nothing about whether media was established, because media runs client-side over WebRTC and the ABS server is never on that path. Do not render it as connected. A NON-HUMAN PRINCIPAL IS REFUSED with 403. An admission policy may legitimately admit an agent as an observer: admission is session eligibility and never permission to hold media, and the only credential this platform can issue carries a speaking capability. Issuing a grant does NOT move the roster and writes NO participation fact. Gated on communication_sessions_update, the same coarse gate the admission verbs use.

post.summary: Withdraw a participant's media before it expires
post.description: The enforcement half of 'authority is current' in the media plane: a participant who should no longer be carrying media loses transport now rather than whenever a token happens to expire. IT IS COARSER THAN IT LOOKS, and that is the vendor's shape rather than a choice: Azure Communication Services offers no per-token revocation, so this withdraws EVERY credential issued to that principal on that resource. A participant who never held a grant is a 200, not a 404: no provider identity means no credential was ever issued, so the post-condition already holds. A 5xx here means the outcome could NOT be established and the credential may still be live. Nothing has been recorded as revoked, and calling again is the correct response — revocation is idempotent and converges. Gated on communication_sessions_update.

post.summary: Admit a participant and mint a join ticket
post.description: THE MINT CHECKPOINT. Evaluates the caller's CURRENT authority for this roster row and, when the server-side admission policy allows it, issues a single-use short-lived join ticket whose plaintext is disclosed EXACTLY ONCE, in this response, and only after the ticket row is durably committed. Store it nowhere and log it nowhere. NO POLICY KEY IS ACCEPTED FROM THE CALLER: a surface asks to join, it does not assert that it may, so the admission authority is resolved server-side from this deployment's configuration and defaults to DENY. Every decision, grant or refusal, appends its own immutable evidence row — a 403 here is a recorded decision you can afterwards ask this API to explain. Gated on communication_sessions_update as a coarse endpoint gate; the real authority is the admission policy.

post.summary: Refuse a participant's admission, on an operator's authority
post.description: THE DELIBERATE HUMAN COUNTERPART OF Admit. It appends a refusal to the SAME immutable admission-evidence trail every automated verdict lands in — the same row type, the same Refused verdict — and it is told apart from a policy verdict by exactly two columns: AuthorityKey carries the operator authority instead of a policy key, and DecisionCode carries abs.communications.admission.operator.denied instead of a policy token. There is deliberately no second rejection record type: splitting the trail would make every reader merge two tables, and the reader that forgot would answer 'why could I not join' with half the truth. NO ADMISSION POLICY IS CONSULTED, because there is nothing to ask — the operator is the authority. IT RECORDS, IT DOES NOT BLOCK: the roster row is untouched and no later admission is barred, because a stored decision is history rather than standing authority in BOTH directions. To take a principal out of the occasion, use Remove. NOTE THE STATUS. Unlike Admit — where a refusal means the CALLER was not let in and answers 403 — a successful denial answers 200 with the decision record, because the operator asked for the refusal to be recorded and it was. 'Your denial was denied' is not what happened. Gated on communication_sessions_update, the same gate Admit uses: allowing and refusing one roster row are two halves of one authority.

THE REDEEM CHECKPOINT. Spends a presented ticket — but only after re-resolving the current principal, tenant, membership, session and participant and RE-EVALUATING the current admission policy from scratch. Minted at 12:00, authority revoked at 12:01, redeemed at 12:02 is a DENIAL: a ticket proves CONTINUITY of an earlier admission attempt and never carries durable authority. A replay FAILS rather than repeating, and two concurrent redemptions resolve to exactly one winner. The ticket travels in the BODY and never in the URL, because a query string is logged by proxies, kept in browser history and echoed into referrers. The response is an admitted-session handoff RealTime consumes; it carries no provider room, no vendor credential and no media grant, because the provider plane is a later slice and signalling is RealTime's.

get.description: The immutable admission-evidence trail for one session — the answer to 'why could I not join'. Every decision at both checkpoints is APPENDED here with the authority that decided, a frozen decision code, the reason and the timestamp, because a denial nobody recorded is a denial nobody can explain. THESE ROWS ARE HISTORY, NEVER STANDING AUTHORITY: 'latest admission == Allowed' is not a test of current admissibility, and no consumer may use it as one. A denial at 12:00 and an admission at 12:05 are two historical facts, not one row that changed its mind.
Counts the session's admission-evidence rows over the same parent-bound specification.

Lists what actually happened at runtime inside one session - who joined, dropped, came back, left or changed the media they were carrying. Distinct from the roster (who BELONGS to the session) and from the admission trail (what an authority DECIDED). Each row says whether ABS observed the fact itself or a provider reported it, and carries both the instant it happened and the instant ABS recorded it. Tenant- and session-scoped by specification, shaped at the database by a projection, OData-shaped through the $-prefixed query string, and gated on communication_sessions_read inside the use case.

Counts the session's participation facts over the SAME specification the list uses, so a badge count can never drift from the list it counts. Honours $filter and $search only - paging must never alter a total.

The "why was I dropped" read: one roster row's runtime timeline within one session. Served by its own participant-bound index rather than by filtering the session's whole stream, which on the highest-volume table in this lane is the difference between a page and a scan.
Counts one roster row's participation facts over the same participant-bound specification.

get.summary: List the tenant's communication provider registrations
get.description: Lists the registrations this tenant OWNS and can administer. Instance-owned resources the platform provides on the tenant's behalf are deliberately not in this list. Shaped at the database by a projection and OData-shaped through the $-prefixed query string. Gated on communication_sessions_read. CredentialReference is an OPAQUE COORDINATE, never a secret value.

post.summary: Register a tenant-owned communication provider resource
post.description: Registers a provider resource the TENANT owns and provides. There is no ownership field on the payload: ownership comes from the authenticated caller, and the instance-owned path is a separate factory no request-shaped type can reach. ProviderKey is resolved SERVER-SIDE against the set this host composes (see GET /Composition); an unknown key is refused rather than defaulted. CredentialReference is an OPAQUE COORDINATE resolved through credential custody: a key, token or connection string posted here would be persisted at rest by definition, and there is deliberately no free-text configuration field to smuggle one through. The registration is created DISABLED; turning it on is a separate act. Gated on communication_sessions_manage rather than _create, because a role that may start meetings must not thereby decide which vendor carries every meeting in the tenant. RETURNS WHAT THE SERVER DECIDED: the id it assigned, the ownership it derived and the status it chose.

get.summary: Count the tenant's communication provider registrations
get.description: Counts over the SAME specification the list uses, so a badge count can never drift from the list it counts. Honours $filter and $search only, because paging must never alter a total.

Reads one registration this tenant may SEE: its own, or the instance-owned resource the platform provides on its behalf. Strictly a read. The tenant rides IN the lookup, so a foreign registration is not merely refused, it is not addressable and the answer is 404.

put.summary: Edit a communication provider registration the caller owns
put.description: Edits the display name, the opaque credential coordinate, the external resource coordinate and the enabled capabilities. Ownership, provider key and purpose CANNOT be edited: a registration changing hands is a new registration, and re-pointing the provider underneath a session already bound to it would make the sticky-binding guarantee a lie. Status cannot be edited here either - turning a provider on is a deliberate act with its own endpoint. The tenant-owned lookup cannot see an instance-owned registration at all, so trying to edit one answers 404. Gated on communication_sessions_manage.

get.summary: List provider effect attempts whose outcome could not be established
get.description: WHAT IS STUCK. Every consequential call this tenant's sessions made against a communication provider whose outcome is NOT settled: a room that may exist and cannot be named, a credential that should be dead and may still be live, a call that began and was never classified. Two states qualify - Attempting (in flight, or stranded under a worker that died) and OutcomeUnknown (already quarantined, exits only on a provider receipt or an operator decision). Settled attempts are excluded: Effected and Refused are ESTABLISHED and need nobody. THIS IS A REPORT AND NEVER A GUARD. Nothing in the provider protocol reads it, and reading it settles nothing - resolving an unsettled attempt is an operator decision, not a side effect of looking. NON-SECRET FIELDS ONLY. No access token, join credential or connection secret is persisted anywhere in this lane, so none can be returned. ProviderEvidence - the free-text vendor response - is deliberately NOT projected: it is the one column whose content the platform does not shape, and a list endpoint is the wrong place to publish it. The SESSION is one hop away rather than on the row: an attempt is keyed on a BINDING, which carries no navigation by design, so read the binding named by BindingId to reach the session. Shaped at the database by a projection and OData-shaped through the $-prefixed query string; the default order is oldest first, because the thing stuck longest is the thing most likely to matter. Gated on communication_sessions_read.

get.summary: Ask whether a provider registration can carry a session for named capabilities
get.description: CONFIGURED AND USABLE ARE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS, and this endpoint answers both without collapsing either into one boolean. It reports six named facts - configured, credential declared, credential resolvable, provider composed in this process, capability enabled, policy eligible - then derives TWO verdicts from them: IsConfigurationReady, the registration's own health, which needs no capability set; and IsUsableForRequestedCapabilities, which is meaningless without one. Three of the six facts are observed per request rather than stored, so the answer cannot go stale and is deliberately not projectable from the database. REQUIREDCAPABILITIES IS MANDATORY AND HAS NO DEFAULT. Omitting it returns 400 rather than an unqualified verdict: with nothing required every capability check passes vacuously, so a registration that can carry no session at all would be reported as usable - mathematically consistent and operationally dangerous. The requested set is ECHOED BACK on the answer, so a caller can never misread which question was answered. Gated on communication_sessions_read.

post.summary: Turn a communication provider registration on
post.description: Marks the registration administratively enabled, which makes it ELIGIBLE for selection. It does not make it usable: credential resolvability, provider composition, capability enablement and policy eligibility are separate facts, and Readiness is where the derived answer lives. Gated on communication_sessions_manage.

post.summary: Turn a communication provider registration off
post.description: Removes the registration from FUTURE selection. It does NOT reach back into sessions already bound to it: a binding is sticky for the life of its session, so a live conversation keeps the resource it was admitted onto and the change takes effect for the next one. Gated on communication_sessions_manage.

post.summary: Temporarily withhold a communication provider registration
post.description: Suspension is kept distinct from disablement because the two mean different things to whoever reads the console later: Disabled is a deliberate indefinite decision, Suspended is a temporary withholding for billing, an incident or an investigation. Collapsing them would lose the reason at exactly the moment somebody is asking why nothing works. Gated on communication_sessions_manage.

get.summary: Read the durable provider bindings a session holds
get.description: DURABLE FACTS ONLY. A session holds at most one binding per purpose - media and telephony are separate seams with separate credentials and a separate regulatory posture, and a tenant may answer them with different vendors. Vendor access tokens, participant grants and short-lived join credentials are EPHEMERAL: they are issued per authorized request and never persisted, so none can be read back here. Parent-bound and tenant-bound, so a binding from another session is not addressable. Gated on communication_sessions_read.

post.summary: Bind a session to a provider resource
post.description: THE CALLER DOES NOT NAME A REGISTRATION, AND CANNOT. There is no registration id on this route, on the body or on the binder's own request type: a caller that could name one could choose whose credentials and whose bill fund the session, and could point a tenant's meeting at another tenant's resource. The request expresses BUSINESS INTENT - which session, for what purpose, needing which capabilities - and the SERVER resolves the effective registration from the tenant, the session, configured policy, the available registrations, their ownership, current authorization and the whole readiness answer. REQUIRED capabilities fail closed; PREFERRED ones degrade. THE BINDING IS STICKY for the life of the session: calling this again returns the binding that already exists rather than choosing again, because a configuration change mid-session must not put half the participants on one vendor and issue the rest credentials for another. Exactly one binding can exist per session per purpose, enforced by a unique constraint rather than by an existence check, so two replicas racing the same session are arbitrated by the database and the loser adopts the winner's row. C5 CREATES NO VENDOR RESOURCE: this claims the binding and returns it in Binding state; recording an external resource coordinate against it is the adapter slice's. Gated on communication_sessions_update, the same permission Admit uses, because getting media for a session is part of the join protocol every attendee performs rather than administration of the tenant's configuration.

get.description: What this host's Communications engine is actually composed of: the media provider codes, the telephony provider codes, the admission policy keys, whether the deny floor and the no-vendor media floor are present, and any defect the startup validator found. It is the operator's answer to 'is the deny default really in this process', asked after the fact rather than by having been watching the console at boot. Tenant-gated on communication_sessions_read: which admission authorities a host has registered is reconnaissance in the wrong hands.
